title: Delegates are required to maintain independence while being appointed, paid and renewed at the Spark Foundation's sole discretion
content:
The Delegation Framework asks Delegates to be two incompatible things.

A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.1 defines a Delegate as a representative "expected to vote in the long-term best interest of the Spark ecosystem," and A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.3.6 makes **Maintain Independence** an enumerated responsibility whose breach is grounds for offboarding.

Every lever over that Delegate, however, sits with the Spark Foundation:

- **Entry** — A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.2.6: the Foundation "may approve or deny any application at any time, for any reason or no stated reason," *even if the applicant satisfies the minimum requirements*, "is not required to provide individualized rationale," and decisions "are final."
- **Continuation** — A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.3: fixed six-month terms with automatic offboarding absent Foundation re-approval.
- **Pay** — A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.6: USD 4,000 per calendar month from the Foundation's own budget, which the Foundation "may withhold or claw back... for non-performance or breach," judged against responsibilities it interprets.

A delegate whose income, tenure and eligibility all depend on an unreviewable discretionary judgment by one entity has a structural incentive to avoid voting against that entity — which is exactly the dependence the independence clause forbids. The framework contains no counterweight: no appeal, no token-holder override of a denial, no compensation source outside the Foundation.

In Atlas terms this is a weak Alignment Artifact for the delegate role. Correct behaviour requires the delegate to supply Inner Incentive — voting against the interests of their own paymaster — rather than being made safe by structure. The framework's own text acknowledges the shape of the problem ("No Waiver of Oversight," A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.6 item 5) while addressing only the reverse direction: that pay does not buy leniency, not that pay does not buy compliance.
description: A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.3.6 mandates independence, yet A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.2.6 lets the Foundation deny or approve for any or no stated reason, with USD 4,000/month subject to Foundation clawback.
